verses.1: The words that came from Jehovah to Jeremiah were these:
verses.2: Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the rulers of Jerusalem.
verses.3: And you said to them, “As the LORD God of Israel says: ‘Let that man be punished, who does not listen to the words of this covenant.’”
verses.4: I commanded your mothers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt from the iron gates, saying, “Hear my voice and do all that I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God.”
verses.5: So that I may establish the covenant I have made with your ancestors, so that they may receive land that is full of milk and herbs, just as it is today. And I swear by Jehovah.
verses.6: And the LORD said to me, “Call all these words aloud in the cities of Judah and in the districts of Jerusalem. Say, ‘Hear the words of this covenant, and obey them.’”
verses.7: For I have testified about your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, and even to this very day, when they hear my voice.
verses.8: And they did not hear, nor pay attention to what was said to them. They went along with their evil hearts. I will bring upon them all the words of this covenant that I commanded them to do, but they did not do them.
verses.9: And the LORD said to me, “There will be found among the people of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem a person who will do evil.”
verses.10: They returned to the ways of their ancient ancestors, who refused to listen to my words. And those ancestors followed other gods and worshiped them. They violated my covenant with Israel and Judah, the covenant I made with their ancestors.
verses.11: Therefore, the LORD said, “I will bring them calamity, because they cannot escape from it. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.”
verses.12: And they went to the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. They cried out to God, who was their savior, but he did not save them during their times of trouble.
verses.13: For from the number of your ancestors, you were born as Jews. And from the number of Jerusalem’s people, you became a place where idols were set up and used as objects of worship.
verses.14: And you shall not pray for this people, nor shall you offer them any sacrifices or prayers. For I do not hear their calls to me when they pray on their own behalf.
verses.15: What can I do for my friend in my house? The many preparations have been made, and they will pass over you. Because of your troubles, I will help you.
verses.16: May the light of the sun be beautiful and fruitful. May Jehovah’s name be praised by those who hear it. May fire be kindled upon it, and may its rays shine brightly.
verses.17: And the Lord, who is the Almighty, will speak evil against you because of the evil that has happened in the houses of Israel and Judah. They have done things that have caused me to be angry, so that I might destroy them completely.
verses.18: And Jehovah will know me, and I will know him also when he sees me among his people.
verses.19: And I, like a fool, tried to do good deeds, but I didn’t know that those thoughts were actually evil ones. They destroyed the trees in their midst, and we were banished from this land of life. Their names will never be remembered again.
verses.20: And Jehovah, your army, will judge with justice. I will see your vengeance against them, for I have delivered you from your enemies.
verses.21: Therefore, as Jehovah has said, “Let not the names of Jehovah be profaned, and let no death come into our hands.”
verses.22: Therefore, thus said Jehovah, the God of hosts: “I will deal with them who are chosen. Their sons and daughters will die in famine.”
verses.23: And they shall not be treated as if I were to bring harm upon those who are in need.
